layout_dets.text: Figure 1. We pose a novel problem: automatically associating subjects in videos with effects' related to them in the scene. Given an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: input video (top) and rough masks of subjects of interest (middle), our method estimates an omnimatte – an alpha matte and foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: color that includes the subject itself along with all scene elements associated with it (bottom). The associated elements can be other objects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: attached to the subject or moving with it, or complex effects such as shadows, reflections, smoke, or ripples the subject creates in water.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Computer vision is increasingly effective at segmenting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: objects in images and videos; however, scene effects re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lated to the objects—shadows, reflections, generated smoke,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: etc.—are typically overlooked. Identifying such scene ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fects and associating them with the objects producing them

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is important for improving our fundamental understanding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of visual scenes, and can also assist a variety of applica-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions such as removing, duplicating, or enhancing objects in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video. In this work, we take a step towards solving this novel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: problem of automatically associating objects with their ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fects in video. Given an ordinary video and a rough seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentation mask over time of one or more subjects of inter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: est, we estimate an omnimatte for each subject—an alpha

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matte and color image that includes the subject along with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: all its related time-varying scene elements. Our model is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained only on the input video in a self-supervised manner,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without any manual labels, and is generic—it produces om-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nimattes automatically for arbitrary objects and a variety

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of effects. We show results on real-world videos contain-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing interactions between different types of subjects (cars,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: animals, people) and complex effects, ranging from semi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transparent elements such as smoke and reflections, to fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: opaque effects such as objects attached to the subject.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: "And first he will see the shadows best, next the reflec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions of men and other objects in the water, and then the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: objects themselves, then he will gaze upon the light of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moon and the stars and the spangled heaven ... Last of all

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: he will be able to see the sun." – Plato

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Is it possible to automatically determine all the effects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: caused by a subject in a video? Reflect for a moment on the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: difficulty of the task: a subject, such as a human wander-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing through a scene, can cast shadows on the floor and dis-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tant walls, and be reflected in windows and other surfaces.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: These effects' are non-local. However, they are correlated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with the subject's shape, motion and, in the case of reflec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions, appearance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Tackling this problem is the objective of this paper. More

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specifically, given an input video and (possibly rough) seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mentations over time of subjects of interest in the video, we

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seek to produce an output opacity matte (alpha matte) for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each subject that includes the subject and their effects in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the scene (Figure 1). We call this the “omnimatte" of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subject. We additionally produce a color background image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: containing the static background elements in the video. We

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieve this by proposing a network and training framework

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that is able to automatically determine and segment regions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that are correlated with the given subject (Figure 2). The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model is trained in a self-supervised way only on the in-

layout_dets.text: Figure 2. Estimating omnimattes from video. The input to the model is an ordinary video with multiple moving objects, and a rough

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation mask M for each object (left). In a pre-processing step, we compute an optical flow field F between consecutive frames

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using [28]. For each object, we pass the mask, estimated flow in the object's region, and a sampled noise image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (representing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background) to our model, producing an omnimatte (color + opacity) and an optical flow field for the object (right). In addition, the model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: predicts a single background color image for the entire video (top), given a spatial texture noise image Z as input. See Sec. 3 for details.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: put video, without observing any additional examples. Our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: solution is inspired by the recent work of Lu et al. [17]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that presented a method to decompose a video into a set of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: human-specific RGBA layers. We generalize this technique

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to support arbitrary objects, by relying only on binary input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: masks (no object-specific representation or processing) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: incorporating general optical flow to account for motion and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frame-to-frame correspondence.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Associating objects with their effects not only improves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: our fundamental understanding of visual scenes and events

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: captured in video, it can also support a range of applica-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions. Consider for example the problem of removing a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: person or other types of objects from a video. As is well

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: known, a common error in person removal, e.g., by inpaint-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing, is that a shadow or reflection of the person remains,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resulting in a video left with just a shadow of the former

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: self’. The erroneous missing of a reflection is a central plot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: point in the film Rising Sun' (1993), and the converse, a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lack of reflection, a common trope of vampire movies. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: important point is that manipulating an object in a video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires dealing not only with the object; its effects in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scene need to be adjusted together with the object in order

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to create realistic and faithful renditions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We demonstrate results of inferring omnimattes for dif-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferent objects such as animals, cars, and people, capturing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a variety of complex scene effects including shadows, re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flections, dust and smoke. We evaluate the resulting om-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nimattes qualitatively and quantitatively, and also demon-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: strate how omnimattes can be useful for video editing ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plications such as object removal, background replacement,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: "color pop", and stroboscopic photography.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Video layer decomposition Our work is inspired by sem-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inal works on layered video decomposition such as [30]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and [6]. Layered representations of images and videos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have been applied widely in computer vision and graphics,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for example, for inferring occlusion relationships (e.g. [6]),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depth (e.g. [39, 27]), and synthesizing novel views (e.g. [26,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 29]). In particular, our work builds on the recent work of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Lu et al. [17] that presented a method for decomposing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a video into a set of human-specific RGBA layers, where

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: each layer represents a person and their associated scene

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elements. They take a neural rendering approach and rep-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resent the geometry and texture of people explicitly, using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a dedicated, human-specific pipeline. We demonstrate that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the neural rendering component is in fact unnecessary, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that comparable results can be achieved by providing only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rough segmentation masks and flow as input to the network.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The result is a simpler and more efficient setup that allows

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the model to handle arbitrary moving objects. We compare

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the results with [17] in Sec. 4.5.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Image and video matting Image and video matting tradi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tionally deals with the problem of estimating a foreground

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layer (color + opacity) and a background color image from a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: given image or a video (e.g., [5, 31, 15, 7, 37, 13, 25]). The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: novel problem we propose—estimating an omnimatte

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also aims at estimating color + opacity layers from an input

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: video. However, the key fundamental difference is that om-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nimattes capture not only an object but also all the various

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scene effects that are correlated with the object. None of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the existing matting methods is suitable for performing this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: task: they cannot handle well entirely semi transparent ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jects, typically require accurate trimaps that are generated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manually, and they are often restricted to estimating two

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: layers (background/foreground). In practice, film produc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion uses manual or semi-automatic rotoscoping to create

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mattes with such effects [14]. Our method works automat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ically and generically on natural, ordinary videos that con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tain arbitrary moving objects and scene effects, and requires

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only rough object masks (e.g., see the flamingo example in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig. 1).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Background subtraction Change detection using back-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ground subtraction [20, 9] typically does not produce al-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pha mattes, but binary masks containing all objects and ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fects (such as shadows). Qian and Sezan's “difference mat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ting" work [23] attempts to use background subtraction and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thresholding to produce a foreground matte with a known

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background image, but the results are very sensitive to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thresholding value. [25] recently modernized that approach,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: producing nice quality, continuous-valued alpha mattes but

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: still require a known, clean image of the background. More

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: importantly, background subtraction and difference matting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cannot solve the omnimatte problem when the video has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: multiple objects with effects. In such cases it is not enough

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to detect the effects, each effect must also be associated its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subject. We evaluate our method numerically and compare

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it with background subtraction using a change detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dataset [34] with pixel-level labels for objects and shadows.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Shadow and reflection detection Specialized methods

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: also exist for detecting, removing, or modifying specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: types of effects, such as shadows and reflections. For ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ample, [8] acquire a shadow displacement map by waving

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a stick over different parts of a scene, then use it to synthe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: size realistic shadows that match an object's shape. [2, 3]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decompose natural videos to remove reflections, shadows,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and smoke. More recently, Wang et al. [33] proposed to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: analyze the motion of people in video and use it to pre-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dict depth, occlusion, and lighting/shadow information, to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increase realism of 2D object insertion. Our goal in this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: work is to provide a general technique for inferring all of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a subject's associated effects. However, as shadows are a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: particularly common effect, we compare our results with a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: state-of-the-art shadow detector [32] in Sec. 4.1.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Video Effects Although omnimattes are not explicitly op-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: timized for editing, they can facilitate various video editing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: effects that rely on input object masks, including object re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moval and video completion (e.g. [10, 35]), object cut-and-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: paste (e.g. [15, 31]), color pop, and creation of stroboscopic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: images from video (e.g. [1]). All of these effects can be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: achieved via simple manipulations of the estimated omni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mattes in a post-processing step, or alternatively, by using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the omnimattes as input to existing methods such as video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: completion (e.g. [10]), to save the manual work required for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: marking the object's effects. We demonstrate these results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Sec. 4.1.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. Estimating Omnimattes from Video

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The input to our method is an ordinary video of mov-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing objects, and one or more layers of rough segmentation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: masks that mark the subjects of interest. The output is an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: omnimatte for each input mask layer, consisting of an alpha

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matte (opacity map) and a color image. The model is trained

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: per-video to reconstruct the input in a self-supervised man-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ner, without observing any additional examples.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To accurately reconstruct the input video, the model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: must infer all the time-varying effects (e.g. shadows, reflec-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions) from the input object masks, which do not represent

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: those effects. Our goal is to steer the model to place the as-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sociated effects in the layer of the subject causing them. Lu,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. [17] showed that this association can be achieved by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: showing the network one mask at a time, leveraging the fact

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that an effect is easier to predict from the object mask most

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correlated with it. For example, the mask of the person in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 1 provides more information about its shadow (more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: similar to it in shape, in motion) compared to the mask of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the dog. Therefore (as shown in [17]) the network tends to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learn to predict the person's shadow from the person's mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (thus associating it with the correct layer). We build on this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: training strategy, but design network inputs and losses to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: encourage this solution for general objects.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1. Overview

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 2 illustrates our pipeline. Our model is a 2D U-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Net [24] that processes the video frame by frame. For each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frame, we compute rough object masks using off-the-shelf

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: techniques to mark the major moving objects in the scene.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We group the objects into N mask layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and de-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine a (possibly time-varying) ordering

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for the layers. For

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: example, in a scene with a rider, a bicycle, and several peo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ple in a crowd, we might group the rider and bicycle into

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one layer, while grouping the crowd into a second layer. To

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: equip our model with explicit information about object mo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion and frame-to-frame correspondence, we also compute

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a dense optical flow field,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , between each frame and the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consecutive frame in the video. This flow field is masked

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by the input masks

layout_dets.text: 3.4. Camera Motion and Background

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We assume the background scene is stationary and cam-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: era motion can be modeled by a time-varying homography

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from an unwrapped “canvas" image, as in [30]. The ho-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mographies

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from frame t to the canvas are estimated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: frames and are held fixed. For input to the network, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: color image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , which is then sampled using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to form

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: time-varying background images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: To make the foreground layers aware of the camera mo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion, the input mask layers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is sampled using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to form time-varying noise images

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . This is a similar approach to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: et al. [17], but in our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: case the noise image is not trainable.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Minor stabilization errors, as well as exposure changes,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vignetting, and radial distortion, usually cause slight

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: changes in appearance even for a stationary background. If

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the background is assumed to be entirely static, these sub-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tle shifts in appearance will show up as noise in our om-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nimatte. Such effects, however, tend to have low spatial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and temporal frequency relative to the subject's effects and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: can be safely captured by applying a refinement warp to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the background layer. The refinement warp consists of a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spatially and temporally coarse grid-based warp. We ad-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ditionally apply a grid-based brightness adjustment to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: final composite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . The parameters of the warp

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and brightness adjustment are optimized together with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: network parameters (see SM for additional details).

layout_dets.text: 3.5. Implementation Details

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For all our results, we used Mask R-CNN [12] to seg-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: segment as additional objects. To increase the detail of the

layout_dets.text: 4.1. Qualitative examples on real videos

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 4.2. Object Removal

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our method can be applied to remove a dynamic object

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from a video by either: (i) binarizing our omnimatte and us-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing it as input to a separate video-completion method such

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: as FGVC [10], or by (ii) simply excluding the object's om-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nimatte layer from our reconstruction.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: As shown in Fig. 4(b,e), removing an object but not its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: correlated effects produces an unrealistic result (object re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: moved but its shadow remains). Typically such effects are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: manually annotated to create a conservative binary mask of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the regions to remove (Fig. 4(c)). To show that an omni-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matte can replace manual editing, we derive a binary mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by thresholding our soft alpha at 0.25 and dilating by 20 pix-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: els, and inputting it to FGVC [10]. Fig. 4(c) shows both the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: horse and its shadow are removed, demonstrating that our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: 4.3. Comparison with Shadow Detection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We show qualitative comparisons with a recent state-of-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the-art shadow detection method, ISD [32], a deep-learning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: based method that takes an RGB image as input and pro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duces segments for object-shadow pairs. ISD integrates a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: MaskRCNN-like object detection stage (Detectron2 [36]),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hence it does not require or allow an input mask.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ject (a bench), and where a person's shadow is occluded

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by another object (a dog). Our method successfully han-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: dles and outperforms ISD in both cases. Occlusions and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shadows cast on other objects present particularly difficult

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cases for purely data-driven methods such as ISD, since

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the appearance of the shadow depends on the relative con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: figuration of multiple objects in the scene, presenting a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: combinatorial explosion of scenarios for training. In con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trast, our method analyzes and leverages space-time infor-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mation throughout the entire video to perform these com-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plex object-effects associations.

layout_dets.text: 4.8. Limitations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While our method allows for small deviations from a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: static background via smooth, coarse geometric and pho-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tometric offsets, when the homographies do not accurately

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: represent the background, the omnimattes must correct for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: these errors by including background elements (e.g. rocks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and grass, Fig. 11). Conversely, we cannot separate ob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: jects or effects that remain entirely stationary relative to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: background throughout the video. These issues could be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: addressed by building a background representation that ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plicitly models the 3D structure of the scene (e.g. [4]).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Finally, we observed that different random initializations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the network's weights may occasionally lead to different,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sometimes undesirable, solutions (see supplemental mate-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rial for visualization). We speculate that more reliable con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vergence could be obtained by further optimizing the order

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in which frames are introduced to the model.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. Conclusion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We have posed a new problem: from an input video with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one or more segmented moving subjects, we produce an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: omnimatte for each subject – an opacity map and color im-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: age that includes the subject itself along with the visual ef-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fects related to it. These effects can be reflections of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: subject, shadows they cast, or attached objects. We have

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proposed a network and training framework for solving this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: new problem, and have demonstrated omnimattes produced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: automatically for real-world videos with a variety of objects

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and associated effects. We have also shown how omnimat-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tes can support a variety of video editing applications.
